 RAMESHBHAI CHAGANBHAI PATEL  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ORS.
==========================================================
Appearance:
MS DIVYA RAWAL for MS TEJAL A VASHI(2704) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 for the Respondent(s) No. 2,3,4,5 MR HARDIK SONI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHEEKATI  MANAVENDRANATH ROY  Date : 15/03/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This Special Criminal Application under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code is filed to quash and set aside the report dated 10.1.2017 of respondent no.5, who is officer in-charge of Khatodara Police Station, Surat City, whereby he has refused to register the report lodged by the petitioner as an FIR and to investigate the case on the ground that the dispute is of civil nature and, consequently, sought direction to respondent no.5,
who is Commissioner of Police, Surat, to direct respondent no.2 to register the FIR on the basis of the report dated 19.7.2013 lodged by the petitioner and to investigate the case.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned APP for the respondent-State and the other respondents-police officers.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5235/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined 3.

The grievance of the petitioner, as can be seen from the affidavit filed in support of this application, is that the petitioner has lodged a report dated 19.7.2013 with respondent no.5 alleging commission of certain offences in relation to various lands owned and possessed by the petitioner and the second respondent did not register an FIR on the basis of said report, even though it discloses commission of cognizable offence, on the ground that the dispute is of civil nature and that he has also passed an order/report to this effect on 10.1.2017.
4.

Therefore, the petitioner prayed to quash and set aside the said order dated 10.1.2017 and to direct respondent no.5, Police Commissioner, to instruct respondent No.2 to register an FIR and investigate the case.

5. Learned APP submits, on instructions and as per the report submitted to this effect today, which is taken on record of the Police Sub Inspector, that report lodged by the petitioner was already registered as an FIR long back in 2018 itself being C.R.No.166 of 2018 with Khatodara Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 468, 471, 120-B and 114 of the Indian Penal Code against ten accused in the said case and the accused have approached this Court seeking quash of the said FIR and this Court ordered not to take coercive steps and said quash petition was ultimately allowed by this Court as per order dated 25.9.2023 and the said FIR was quashed.

So, he submits that the allegations made by the petitioner that the police is not registering the FIR and investigating the case is not correct and he prayed for NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5235/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined dismissal of the application.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that FIR relates to offences committed in respect of one landed property owned and possessed by the petitioner and offences are committed in respect of other landed property of the petitioner and the said FIR is not being registered.
7.

If the grievance of the petitioner is that report lodged by the petitioner is not being registered as an FIR and the offence is not being investigated, it is settled law that remedy of the writ petitioner is not by way of filing a writ petition either under Article 226 of the Constitution of India or a petition under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code invoking inherent powers of this Court, and the remedy of the petitioner in the said facts and circumstances of the case is to exhaust various remedies contemplated and provided under Sections 154 (3) and 156 (3) and 200 of CrPC.

The said legal position has been clearly enunciated by the Apex Court in the case of Sakiri Vasu v. State of Uttra Pradesh and Others reported in (2008) 2 SCC 409.
8.

entities.text: Sakiri Vasu v. State of Uttra Pradesh and Others reported in (2008) 2 SCC 409
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Apex Court clearly held that when the grievance of the petitioner is that the report lodged by him is not being registered as an FIR even though it discloses commission of cognizable offence then his remedy is not by way of filing a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution or a petition under Section 482 of CrPC and he has to seek remedy provided in CrPC as discussed supra.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5235/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined Rameshbhai Chaganbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67647700/
2 9.

entities.text: Rameshbhai Chaganbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in view of clear law laid down in the aforesaid judgment of the Apex court, this application is not maintainable and it is liable to be dismissed.
10. Resultantly, this application is dismissed as not maintainable.
However, the petitioner is at liberty to exhaust the remedies provided under Criminal procedure Code, as discussed supra.
